name: Correlations
description: What goes with what in your days: a journal's energy or mood against meetings, booked hours, messages, todos, spending and your other fields — same day and the day after. Computed in code, told only when it holds.
author: Zeff

tools.name: correlations
tools.title: Correlations in the user's days
tools.description: What goes with a daily series in the user's data — e.g. a journal's Energy or Mood against meeting hours, booked hours, messages received/sent, todos, spending, first/last activity and the other fields of their Workspace databases, same day and the day after. Computed in code (Spearman/Pearson, group comparisons, a permutation test with Benjamini–Hochberg); only findings that hold are listed, each as a sentence with n, ρ and the groups' means — quote them as they are. No findings means nothing reliable: say so, don't invent patterns. Give `other` to ask about one pair (answered whether it holds or not).

input.name: database
input.description: The Workspace database's name, e.g. 'Einträge' or 'Journal' (leave out for Zeff's own series like 'Meeting hours').

input.name: field
input.description: The field (property) of that database, e.g. 'Energy' or 'Mood'; a tag as 'Tags: Family'; or a series id.

input.name: days
input.description: The period: the last N days up to `to` (default 90, 14–3650).

input.name: other
input.description: One other series to compare with (its label, e.g. 'Meeting hours' or 'Journal › Tags: Work', or its id).

widgets.label: Correlations
widgets.description: What goes with a field of your days — a journal's energy or mood against meetings, booked hours, messages, spending and your other fields — only what holds, with n.
